newsitem.title: USA: Xerox buys rest of Rank-Xerox, suspends share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Xerox buys rest of Rank-Xerox, suspends share buyback.

text.p: Xerox Corp. said Friday it will pay about $1.5 billion to buy the remaining 20 percent stake in its 41-year-old Rank Xerox office equipment joint venture from Britain's Rank Group Plc.
Xerox suspended a $1 billion stock buyback programme to help fund the acquisition. Other funding sources include free cash flow and proceeds from the sale of its insurance units.
The purchase gives Stamford, Conn.-based Xerox sole ownership of the venture, based in Britain, which will be renamed Xerox Ltd. when the deal closes, the company said.

Xerox and Rank, a leisure and entertainment company, said Xerox would pay 500 million pounds ($812.6 million) on completion of the transaction, expected at the end of June. The balance will be payable in two annual instalments of 220 million pounds ($358 million).
Xerox may pay another 60 million pounds ($98 million) in 2000, based on profit performance by 1999, the companies said.
Salomon Brothers Inc. estimated the price at about 10 times the venture's 1997 earnings.
The transaction has been approved by the boards of both companies, Xerox said.

"Use of the company's financial resources to fund this $1.5 billion transaction produces greater value to Xerox shareholders than continuing the current share repurchase programme," Xerox Chairman Paul Allaire said.
"However, we will revist the share repurchase programme in the future," he added.
To date, the company has paid $406 million for 8.2 million shares since it initiated the $1 billion buyback in 1996.
Rank Xerox manufactures Xerox products, systems and supplies and markets them in more than 80 countries in Europe, Asia and Africa. The venture also owns a 50 percent stake in Fuji Xerox.

Xerox spokesman Judd Everhart said the company has raised its 1997 earnings target in light of the Rank agreement. Its new target for the year is $3.95 per share, up from previous consensus estimates of $3.85. It earned $3.31 per share in 1996.
Everhart said the deal should add 20 cents per share to fiscal 1998 earnings, raising the target to $4.55 per share from $4.35.
The Rank Xerox venture contributed $432 million to Xerox's net income of $1.2 billion in 1996, Everhart said.
Xerox formed the Marlow, England-based joint venture in 1956 and has controlled it since 1969, Everhart said. "We decided to take more over the years," he said.
Rank had been eager to sell its remaining stake as part of its goal of focusing on its core restaurant and entertainment business, Rank and Xerox officials said in separate interviews.

Recognising Rank's willingness to sell, it was just a matter of price, Everhart said. "It was strictly the price," he said. "The price was attractive and we were confident it will not hurt our bottom line."
Wall Street analysts agreed the price was right, and several moved quickly to raise their earnings estimates to be consistent with Xerox's own projections.
"The price was consistent with the 13 percent stake they added from Rank in 1995," said Rudy Hokanson of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. In 1995, Xerox raised its stake from 67 percent to 80 percent.
"This was a real opportunity to enhance shareholder value," he said.
Xerox stock rose 75 cents to $67.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Rank said Friday it intended to repurchase its own shares up to a maximum value of 250 million pounds ($407 million).

The London-based company said it expected to launch a stock buyback later this year and would use the balance of the initial payment from Xerox to cut debt and invest in its leisure and entertainment businesses.
